data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's mechanism asserts additive redundancy makes panel errors uncorrelated while expert errors are systemic, but it never identifies the evidence within a single evaluation that would distinguish genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that tracks the right answer. The problem explicitly requires identifying that evidence; SRC_002 only offers a causal story about error-filtering. Without a discriminator (e.g., item-level agreement patterns or out-of-distribution probes), the observed accuracy could be indistinguishable from rote checklist compliance that happens to track outcomes. Counterexample: two evaluations with identical panel accuracy—one where members independently trigger checklist items and one where members mechanically copy the same checklist path; SRC_002 cannot distinguish them.
